summary: Iteration 3 backend regression: 12/13 pytest cases pass. Covered auth (register/login), guest quota + 4th-scan 401, seeded oats product structure & nutrition_per_100g, REAL Open Food Facts lookup for Nutella (3017620422003) with sugar<=50 / palm<=50 / sugars_g in tolerance of 56, profile PUT/GET persistence, registered entitlements (free_remaining=5 -> 4 after 1 scan), guest->registered history migration via x-guest-id header, contributions (pending_verification), and plans (launch_promo=true, monthly ₹72, yearly ₹450). ONE FAILURE exposes a real algorithm bug: personalized_match on the Calm Barrier Cleanser (contains Fragrance) INCREASES from 66 (baseline, no prefs) to 70 when the user sets dietary=['Vegan'] + sensitivities=['Paraben-free','Fragrance-free'] — the opposite of the intended UX. Root cause is in build_public_product/personalized_match in /app/backend/server.py.

critical.issue: For barcode 8906087771204 (Calm Barrier Cleanser) with Fragrance in the ingredients, applying user prefs dietary=['Vegan']+sensitivities=['Paraben-free','Fragrance-free'] returns personal_match=70 while baseline (no prefs) returns 66. Setting sensitivities that the product VIOLATES makes the score go up. Algorithm in personalized_match() uses base = 55 + ratio*45 which can exceed the raw overall_score, and the min-score penalty only triggers for scores < 25 while fragrance is scored 38, so explicit sensitivity violations are unpenalised. See /app/backend/server.py:309-374.

action_items: Fix personalized_match in /app/backend/server.py so that an explicit sensitivity violation (fragrance / paraben / additive) reduces personal_match below the raw overall_health_score. Suggested: (a) apply an explicit penalty when a sensitivity check fails (e.g. -15 per failed sensitivity), and (b) cap base by overall_score when any sensitivity check is False, and/or (c) widen the min-score penalty threshold from <25 to also cover moderate hazards (score<45) when they violate an explicit avoidance keyword.

Optional: return dietary_type='vegan' or 'not_applicable' consideration for personal_care products so Vegan preference doesn't spuriously fail on cosmetics — currently 'not_applicable' fails the vegan check for a cleanser.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py at 743 lines is close to the 700-line split threshold; consider extracting ingredient DB, scoring, and remote_lookup into modules.
personalized_match uses hardcoded floor 55 which is higher than many valid overall_score values, producing counter-intuitive results (see HIGH bug above).

consume_scan / lookup_product ordering: quota is decremented BEFORE product existence is verified, so 404 lookups still consume a guest scan. Consider deferring consume_scan until after a product is resolved.
remote_lookup uses sync requests inside async handler which will block the event loop; consider httpx.AsyncClient.
Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook increments purchased_balance by quantity metadata sent from the client; validate against the stored payment record instead of trusting metadata.
seed_data_creation: Only transient TEST_ users, guest ids, and history records were created during the run. No changes to seeded products.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_3.py. BASE_URL comes from EXPO_BACKEND_URL (falls back to EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL). Nutella test may skip if Open Food Facts is unreachable. Emails on register are lowercased server-side, so tests must use lowercase-prefixed emails.
rca_of_issue: personalized_match() (server.py:309-374): when preferences are supplied, base = 55 + ratio*45 with a penalty of -12 only when min(scores)<25. For the Calm Barrier Cleanser: ingredients scores = [aqua 90, glycerin 78, sodium laureth sulfate 62 (unknown, neutral), panthenol 78, phenoxyethanol 55, fragrance 38]. With prefs Vegan+ParabenFree+FragranceFree the three checks evaluate to [False, True, False] (vegan fails because dietary_type='not_applicable', paraben passes, fragrance fails because the ingredient list contains 'fragrance'), ratio=1/3, base=70, min(scores)=38 so no penalty → personal_match=70. Baseline path with no prefs falls through to max(40, min(100, int(overall_score))) = max(40, 66) = 66. Hence the paradox: opting into the Fragrance-free sensitivity RAISES the personal_match against a fragranced product. Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/register a fresh user, (2) GET /api/products/lookup?barcode=8906087771204 without prefs → note personal_match, (3) PUT /api/profile {dietary:['Vegan'],targets:[],sensitivities:['Paraben-free','Fragrance-free']}, (4) GET the same lookup again → observe personal_match rises. Mitigation: apply explicit -15 penalty for each False sensitivity check, and/or clamp base = min(base, overall_score) when any sensitivity failed.
